messages.text: What are the most important S-parameters capabilities for applications in Automotive?

Short answer: the most important automotive S-parameter/VNA-related capabilities supported by the passages are high-speed channel characterization, PCB/PCBA signal-integrity testing, material/stackup extraction, cable/connector validation, and multiport VNA scalability for complex RF setups.[1][10][26]
- For high-speed automotive digital links, prioritize transmission-channel validation, measurement-path-to-DUT/test-board validation, and interface testing where network analyzers are listed as relevant instruments.[1]
- For PCB/PCBA signal integrity, prioritize insertion loss, crosstalk, eye-diagram-related validation, and TDR impedance workflows.[1]
- For PCB fabricators and system houses, prioritize material measurement, material/stackup selection, signal-integrity modeling/testing, sampling testing, and production/process monitoring.[10]
- Key measurable features to cover include impedance/TDR, Dk/Df extraction, insertion loss, roughness, crosstalk, transmission-line modeling, eye diagram, Delta-L, ISD/ADK, and cable/connector testing.[10]
- For high-speed SerDes automotive-adjacent interfaces, the source lists GMSL and ASA among high-speed SerDes standards/interfaces, alongside LVDS, HDMI, MIPI, USB, PCIe and others.[1]
- For more complex VNA setups, the R&S ZNA67EXT system consists of one R&S ZNA67 vector network analyzer and up to four external test sets.[26]
- For phased-array antenna module testing, VNAs are used together with vector signal generators and vector signal analyzers in PAAM lifecycle test setups.[28]
- Automotive radar echo generation is covered by AREG800A, but the cited passages describe dynamic artificial object generation rather than S-parameter/VNA capability.[4][8]
